_provenance: c RECALIBRATED 2026-08-26 via reward-scale calibration (superseding the original provisional c=0.1, which was never used in any formal or Priority 1 training run). epsilon remains as originally frozen. Both derived from the same real WSC+Dense trace probe (validation/wsc_dense_trace_probe.py -> validation/wsc_dense_trace_probe_output.jsonl, 73 steps, resumed from the real seed-900101 C64 checkpoint) -- NOT from any training-outcome/fairness/completion/collision comparison, and NOT from any formal Dense training result (none has been run).
excludes: NO exp01 experience_score -- Phi_t is built entirely from thesis.study_b.utility.running_active_attainment + thesis.study_b.welfare_reward.WelfareCondition.welfare_fn, never DER's four-weight aggregate
epsilon_reasoning: UNCHANGED from the original freeze. Observed |DeltaPhi_t| distribution over 72 nonzero steps: min=9.02e-6, median=3.47e-5, p90=5.27e-4, max=1.36e-2. epsilon=1e-6 sits below every observed real transition (>=9x margin below the smallest), at the scale of floating-point rounding noise for a running-average computation, so it filters only numerical noise without swallowing real welfare transitions.
dense_active_frequency_note: p = fraction of the 73 recorded steps where abs(DeltaPhi) > epsilon(1e-6): 70 positive + 2 negative = 72/73 = 0.9863 dense-active, 1/73 = 0.0137 dead-zone. This is very high because epsilon=1e-6 is far below the smallest real DeltaPhi observed (9.02e-6) -- dense shaping fires on nearly every step by design of that epsilon choice, not a bug.

magnitude_recalibration.why_revoked: Actual Study B reward traces showed that c=0.1 would materially dominate the typical non-terminal base reward: median(abs(base_reward)) across all (step, agent) entries in the same trace was only 0.004244, so c=0.1 alone (before even multiplying by dense-active frequency) is ~23.6x that typical per-step reward magnitude -- far outside any defensible 'small nudge' role for a shaping term.
magnitude_recalibration.note_on_scale_source: These are absolute values (abs(base_reward)) per (step, agent) entry across all 4 vehicles x 73 steps = 292 entries, NOT a signed median -- signed values would partially cancel and understate the true magnitude.
magnitude_recalibration.target_interval_derivation: c_10pct = 0.10 * median_abs_base_reward / p = 0.10*0.004244/0.9863; c_25pct = 0.25 * median_abs_base_reward / p = 0.25*0.004244/0.9863.
magnitude_recalibration.selection_rule_applied: Both 0.0005 and 0.001 fall within [c_10pct, c_25pct]; the author's own tie-breaking rule ('prefer the more conservative smaller value when two are both reasonable') selects 0.0005.
magnitude_recalibration.estimated_timestep_ratio_derivation: p * c / median_abs_base_reward = 0.9863 * 0.0005 / 0.004244 = 0.1162 (reported 0.1146 from a slightly different rounding path in the calibration script; both within the 0.10-0.25 target).

episode_level_sanity_check.verdict: Well below the 0.5 danger threshold -- no downgrade to a smaller candidate needed. Caveat: derived from a single episode (the only one in the available trace), so this is a sanity check, not a robust multi-episode estimate.
